transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I'm here because my primary care doctor seems concerned that my meal planning has gotten a bit too tight. 

Though, honestly, to me it just feels like keeping things orderly. I usually just keep breakfast to a yogurt, I'll skip lunch if I’m busy, and then I make a very measured dinner. It's really just a way to make sure the day stays on track and organized, but she felt I needed to come talk to you about it.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight over the past few months, and if so, was that intentional on your part?

Yes, it has gone down. My primary doctor pointed out that my weight has drifted down more than she likes over the last few months. 

As for whether it's intentional... well, I suppose it is. Honestly, when I look at the chart, I still find myself thinking that a little lower would just be a cleaner, more manageable number. It just makes sense to me to keep it there.
Do you ever experience episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time and feel like you've lost control during those moments?

No, I don't really have anything like that. I don't eat large amounts of food at once, and I certainly don't feel out of control with it. Like I said, everything is very measured and planned out. Losing control isn't really an issue for me.
Do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of those things. I don't make myself sick or take laxatives, and I don't exercise all that much, really. Just the usual walking around. The weight loss is really just from keeping my meals small and planned out like I mentioned. I don't feel the need to do anything extra to keep the weight off.
When you look at yourself in the mirror or think about your body, do you feel that you are overweight or too heavy, or are you satisfied with how your body looks?

Well, I know I'm an older woman. I'm not trying to look young or anything like that. But... I still judge how well I'm handling myself by how I look. If my waist and hips look contained in my clothes, then I feel okay. If they don't, I feel like I'm doing something wrong. So, I wouldn't say I'm satisfied, exactly. I just like to keep things neat and controlled.
What is your current height and weight, and has your doctor mentioned what your BMI is or whether your weight is considered below normal for someone your age and height?

I'm about 5 foot 4, and right now I weigh 102 pounds. My regular doctor did bring it up recently, actually. She said my weight has drifted down more than she likes, and that it's below what's considered normal for my height. I think she said my BMI was somewhere in the 17s. 

But... honestly, when I look at the chart, I still find myself thinking that a little lower would just be a cleaner, more manageable number. It just feels more precise to me.
How long has your weight been in this range, and has this pattern of restricted eating been going on for several months or longer?

I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. I haven't really kept track of exactly when my weight got down to this specific number. It feels like I've just been managing my meals this way for a while now... it's just become my regular routine. So I couldn't really give you a specific number of months or an exact timeline for when it started.
When did you first start noticing that your eating patterns became this restricted and organized? Was it within the last few months, or has this been going on for longer than that?

Like I mentioned just a moment ago, I really couldn't give you an exact timeframe. I don't know if it was within the last few months or longer. I haven't been keeping track of when exactly I started eating this way. It's just how I do things now.
Looking back over the past year, would you say this pattern of keeping your meals small and measured has been going on for at least three months or longer?

I know you're trying to pin down a specific timeframe, but... I really just don't have the dates to give you. I suppose it could be three months, or maybe it hasn't been quite that long. I just don't track the calendar for this. I track my food, but not when this all started. So, like I said, I really can't give you a definitive yes or no on that three-month mark.

Can you think back to a specific event or time in your life—like a holiday, a family visit, or something else you remember clearly—when you were definitely eating normally before these restricted meals started?

I'm trying to think back... but honestly, no, nothing really stands out. I don't have a clear memory of a before and after tied to a holiday or a visit or anything like that. 

It wasn't really a sudden switch where I was eating one way at Thanksgiving and then completely different the next week. It just sort of gradually became the way I manage things now. So... no, I can't really point to a specific event for you.

When you think about your current weight of 102 pounds and these small, measured meals you're eating now—compared to how you were eating and your weight a year ago—would you say you've been at this lower weight and eating this way for most of that year, or did it happen more recently within the last several months?

I really couldn't tell you if it's been most of the year or just the last few months. Like I've been saying, I just haven't been paying attention to the timeline of it all. I know I weigh 102 now, and I know how I eat now, but as for when exactly I got to this point compared to a year ago... I just don't have a clear answer for you. It's just where I'm at right now.
